subject.title: Expose structured progress metrics in hook events for plugin-based live progress cards

question: Should OpenClaw add producer-owned structured progress metrics to plugin hook events, and which runtime source owns `stepTotal`, `percent`, ETA, and terminal metrics across embedded, CLI, and Codex paths?
rationale: The code change is feasible, but the public Plugin SDK semantics and progress source of truth are product/API decisions that automation should not invent.

options.title: Define a narrow metrics contract
options.body: Add optional metrics only where the runtime can produce authoritative values, document unknown fields as absent, and cover embedded/CLI/Codex-facing producers with focused tests.

options.title: Keep hooks unchanged
options.body: Leave plugins to derive progress from existing lifecycle and tool events, accepting text-only live cards until a stronger progress source exists.

options.title: Create a separate progress event
options.body: Design a dedicated progress event or agent-event projection instead of attaching percentages to tool and terminal hooks.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow metrics contract
recommendation.body: Add optional metrics only where the runtime can produce authoritative values, document unknown fields as absent, and cover embedded/CLI/Codex-facing producers with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior run/tool hook correlation work makes this the closest current-main ownership trail for a public hook contract decision.
